killed.title: RightsPulse (UGC Usage-Rights & TikTok Spark / Meta Partnership Expiry Guardrail)
killed.stage: Deep Dive — Rude Q&A + Dalio Panel

plausible.justification: Store Leads, AdLibrarySpy, StoreCensus, and DemandSage (2025-2026) report 720k-820k+ Shopify stores with Meta Pixel, 410k-443k+ with TikTok Pixel, ~200k-300k+ U.S. dual-pixel Shopify stores, and ~56k distinct Shopify Plus merchants (28k-30k+ Plus stores with TikTok Pixel), plus WooCommerce/BigCommerce/custom DTC brands. Narrowing to scaling DTC brands actively running 15+ creator-backed ads with expiring TikTok Spark codes or time-limited Meta Partnership/UGC licenses lands at 100k (1M exceeds total global Shopify Meta-Pixel stores; 10k is below the 28k-30k+ Shopify Plus TikTok-Pixel cohort alone). Paid-social agencies (~35.5k Clutch US / ~326k global digital agencies, ~10k-30k DTC paid-social specialists) are excluded as a separate Scenario B buyer.

self_aware.justification: Threads on r/TikTokAds, r/UGCcreators, and r/ecommerce alongside UsageHawk, UGC Roster, and Archive reports show thought-leaders, talent managers, and previously burned brands care acutely about Spark flatlines (4025) and Meta Ad Library overrun invoices. However, day-to-day expiry enforcement is not industry-standard practice (0.5): Reddit and industry guides note few brands track license dates consistently, many assume active Meta handles imply perpetual rights or rely on ad-hoc Sheets, and DTC growth teams prioritize ROAS and creative output until burned once (knowing-but-not-prioritizing, matching the WP Engine 0.1 anchor).

lucrative.justification: Live 2025-2026 pricing confirms DTC paid-social brands allocate $1k/yr-tier credit-card budgets to single-wedge creative/rights ops SaaS: direct standalone rival ugcrightstracker.com charges $49/mo Starter ($588/yr), $129/mo Growth ($1,548/yr), and $299/mo Agency ($3,588/yr); Lumanu starts at $99/mo ($1,188/yr) + payout fees; Foreplay charges $59-$175/mo ($708-$2,100/yr); Atria $129/mo annual ($1,548/yr); Modash $299/mo; Insense/UGC Roster $400-$800+/mo; Motion/Archive ~$1,000/mo. RightsPulse's $99/mo ($990/yr) sits cleanly at $1k/yr (vs $100/yr creator-side apps), though interviews must test resistance vs $49/mo manual trackers.

liquid.justification: Read-only OAuth monitoring requires no multi-year rip-and-replace for Sheets/Airtable users (ruling out 0.01), but fails 1.0 ('always in the market'): compliance guardrails are priority-#7 purchases typically triggered episodically/annually (after a Spark flatline, a Meta Ad Library breach invoice, or a pre-BFCM creative ops cleanup), require upfront backfill of existing creator contracts/dates, and face annual contract windows for brands already on Archive, Insense, GRIN, or Aspire.

eager_identity.justification: Per DP37, 0.5 ('indifferent, no red flags') is the honest baseline for self-serve credit-card SaaS sold to DTC e-commerce growth teams. Strictly read-only OAuth (Meta ads_read, TikTok identity/video/info), zero ad-spend write mutations, zero consumer PII, zero payout custody, and full CSV exportability avoid DP10 institutional trust walls (SOC 2, Entra Admin Consent, HIPAA). Meta/TikTok App Review and Business Verification are founder execution hurdles rather than buyer-side refusal. Not 1.0 for an unvetted indie founder.

eager_comparative.justification: Direct standalone rival UGC Rights Tracker ($49-$299/mo) and DIY Sheets/Airtable are manual databases with email reminders—they do not read Meta ads_read or TikTok identity/video/info auth_end_time to detect live ad spend on expired rights across duplicated ad sets or trigger zero-login creator renewal links. Marketplaces (Insense $400-$800+/mo + 7-20%, UGC Roster $499-$1,249/mo + 5%) structurally avoid monitoring off-platform creators; creative tools (Foreplay $59-$175/mo, Atria $129+/mo, Motion $999/mo) track ROAS/swipes not license expiry; enterprise suites (Archive ~$1k/mo, GRIN/Aspire $20k-$54k/yr) cost 10x-50x more; creator tools (UsageHawk) lack brand ad-account APIs. Caveat: automatic Meta matching applies cleanly to Partnership Ads (brand-handle uploaded UGC still needs naming/asset mapping) and Billo perpetual buyouts bypass Meta expiry, ruling out 1.0 but earning 0.5 under DP36.

enduring.justification: Scaling DTC paid-social teams onboard fresh creator batches monthly with rolling 30/60/90/180/365-day usage terms and TikTok Spark codes, creating a genuinely recurring monitoring problem (0.5). Not 1.0 because a read-only monitor with portable CSV exports has minimal switching lock-in—brands that pause TikTok/whitelisting spend, shift to perpetual buyouts, or cut SaaS spend in slow quarters can cancel easily.

plausible.justification: Changed from 100k -> 10k. Store Leads and StoreCensus (2025-2026) report ~56,000 distinct Shopify Plus merchants globally (~28k-30k+ Plus stores with TikTok Pixel). Narrowing strictly to 8-figure ($10M-$100M/yr) DTC e-commerce brands spending $50k-$500k+/mo on 50-200+ active Meta Partnership Ads and TikTok Spark Ads across multiple creator sources (agencies + direct creators + marketplaces) lands cleanly at 10k globally (100k exceeds all distinct Shopify Plus merchants; 1k is far too small).

self_aware.justification: Changed from 0.1 -> 0.5. At 8-figure Shopify Plus scale ($50k-$500k+/mo paid social, 50-200+ active creator licenses), industry workflow analyses (pitchlo.com, topgrowthmarketing.com, influenceflow.com, usagehawk.com) confirm structured usage-rights expiration tracking and renewal loops are industry-standard practice: these brands employ dedicated creative/influencer ops leads, standardize 30/90/180-day licensing clauses, and are the primary target of talent-agency Meta Ad Library compliance audits.

lucrative.justification: Changed from $1k -> $10k (repriced to $499/mo = $5,988/yr, nearly 2x the $3,162 log-midpoint between $1k and $10k). Live 2025-2026 benchmarks confirm 8-figure Shopify Plus brands demonstrably allocate $5k-$18k+/yr to single-pillar paid-social creative/rights ops tools: Archive (~$12k/yr), Motion ($12k+/yr), Atria Plus/Business ($5.7k-$11.5k/yr), Insense/Cohley ($6k-$18k+/yr + fees), Dash/Bynder ($12k-$42k/yr), and GRIN/Aspire ($20k-$54k/yr), where preventing one $10k+ breach invoice or $3k/day Spark flatline pays for the year. Believability is honestly capped at 0.4 because direct standalone rival ugcrightstracker.com prices at $129-$299/mo ($1.5k-$3.6k/yr), creating high uncertainty on whether standalone read-only monitoring holds $499/mo in buyer interviews.

liquid.justification: Unchanged at 0.1. Read-only OAuth avoids multi-year rip-and-replace lock-in, but at $499/mo ($5,988/yr) 8-figure DTC brands still purchase compliance guardrails episodically/annually (post-breach invoice, post-Spark outage, or during pre-BFCM/annual ops audits), face upfront backfill of 50-200+ active creator agreements across agencies and marketplaces, and evaluate overlap against annual Archive, Insense, GRIN, or Aspire renewals.

eager_identity.justification: Unchanged at 0.5. $10M-$50M/yr Shopify Plus DTC brands (typically 15-80 employees, VP of Growth/Paid Social with corporate card authority) routinely buy $450-$999/mo OAuth SaaS (Foreplay $459/mo, Atria $479-$959/mo, Motion $999/mo, Cruva/Reacher $599/mo) without Fortune 500 SOC 2 procurement walls, and strictly read-only Meta ads_read + TikTok identity/video/info with zero consumer PII, zero write mutations, and portable CSV/PDF exports avoid DP10 institutional walls. Caveat: an unvetted indie founder charging $499/mo for compliance monitoring faces sharper durability/missed-alert scrutiny than at $99/mo (must exclude $100M+ Fortune 500 enterprises where SOC 2 drops this to 0.1).

eager_comparative.justification: Unchanged at 0.5. At 8-figure scale, brands source creators simultaneously from agencies, direct DMs, marketplaces, and TikTok Shop affiliates—leaving walled-garden marketplaces (Insense/Cohley $400-$1,500+/mo + 7-20% fees) structurally blind to off-platform creators. Direct rival ugcrightstracker.com ($129-$299/mo) lacks live Meta ads_read and TikTok identity/video/info spend detection; Motion ($999/mo) and Atria ($479-$959/mo) track ROAS not contract expiry; GRIN/Aspire ($20k-$54k/yr) rely on manual custom-field tagging; enterprise DAMs (Dash/Bynder $12k-$42k/yr) lack live ad-account enforcement. Caveat: non-Partnership Meta UGC still requires naming/asset mapping, and Archive (~$1k/mo) or Motion could add expiry API alerts later.

enduring.justification: Unchanged at 0.5. 8-figure DTC brands continuously refresh dozens of creator assets monthly across US/international ad accounts with rolling 30/60/90/180/365-day contracts and Spark codes, making rights enforcement a permanent recurring operational problem. Not 1.0 because read-only monitoring with exportable audit logs lacks hard system-of-record lock-in if an incumbent (Archive, Motion, Foreplay) bundles live expiry checks.

scenario_b.band: VIABLE INDIE (>= 1.0 — can sustain an indie company)

plausible.justification: Held at 10,000. Store Leads, StoreCensus, and BuiltWith put active Shopify Plus storefronts at ~56k-85k globally (~77% above $1M/yr, with a smaller verified subset clearing $10M+/yr). Narrowed strictly to 8-figure ($10M-$100M/yr) multi-source DTC brands running 50-200+ active creator ads across Meta and TikTok, 10,000 globally is the honest coarse order-of-magnitude tier—leaving zero margin for any other factor slipping.

self_aware.justification: Held at 0.5. 8-figure DTC brands with dedicated creative/influencer ops leads are demonstrably aware of creator usage-rights expirations and TikTok Spark outages, evidenced by perpetual-buyout terms on Insense/Cohley, usage-rights modules on Archive/Air.inc, and Meta Ad Library overage audits via UsageHawk (usagehawk.com). Problem awareness is real; standalone WTP and defensibility fail.

lucrative.justification: Conceded $10,000 -> $1,000. Direct standalone competitor ugcrightstracker.com is live at $49/mo (Starter, 30 rights), $129/mo (Growth, 150 active rights, 5 clients), and $299/mo (Agency, unlimited clients & unlimited rights = $3,588/yr) with a 14-day free trial. The original pitch itself priced RightsPulse at $99/mo ($990/yr) Brand and $249/mo ($2,490/yr) Agency. Repricing the identical read-only notifier 5x to $499/mo ($5,988/yr) by comparing it to full operational systems of record (Archive ~$12k/yr, Motion $12k/yr, Insense/Cohley $6k-$18k/yr) was scorecard back-solving. Realistic standalone WTP sits in the $1,000/yr Fermi tier ($99-$249/mo, below the $3,162 log-midpoint).

liquid.justification: Unchanged at 0.1. Brands adopt usage-rights monitoring episodically (after a breach invoice, Spark outage, or annual ops audit), face heavy upfront contract backfill across scattered agency PDFs, DMs, and marketplaces, and evaluate overlap against annual Archive, Insense, GRIN, or Aspire renewals.

eager_identity.justification: Held at 0.5 strictly under honest self-serve mid-market pricing ($99-$249/mo, DP37) where $10M-$50M DTC growth teams connect OAuth to boutique tools without Fortune 500 SOC 2 procurement walls. Explicitly noted that Scenario B's inflated $499/mo legal-compliance positioning for $50M-$100M brands would drag an unvetted solo founder without SOC 2, E&O insurance, or logos down to 0.1 due to ad-account trade-secret exposure and legal-indemnification expectations.

eager_comparative.justification: Conceded 0.5 -> 0.1. Primary docs and live rivals eliminate any incumbent-uncopyable trade-off (DP17, DP26, DP36): Meta Marketing API ads_read (developers.facebook.com) exposes no Partnership Ad code expiration field and zero creator identity for brand-handle uploaded or multi-creator mashup UGC videos, forcing manual naming and contract double-entry; Insense (insense.pro), Billo, and Cohley (cohley.com) grant perpetual digital usage rights as standard; TikTok Business Center Partner Authorization ($0) and 365-day Spark codes shrink expiry outages (business-api.tiktok.com); Archive (archive.com) bundles Usage Rights, Whitelisting, and Spark Codes while Air.inc handles expiry metadata and native Meta Ad Set End Dates / Automated Rules (plus Bïrch) actually pause expired ads for $0; and direct standalone rival ugcrightstracker.com ($49-$299/mo) or incumbents Motion/Archive face zero business-model barrier to copying a read-only API poller.

enduring.justification: Unchanged at 0.5. Rolling creator licensing and Spark code renewals recur continuously for scaling DTC brands, but a disconnected read-only monitoring sidecar with exportable logs has zero system-of-record lock-in and churns immediately once Archive, Motion, or ugcrightstracker.com bundles expiry alerts.

killed.reason: BAD_IDEA — KILL SCENARIO B AND STANDALONE RIGHTSPULSE. The Advocate made a clean, candid fatal concession across both challenged Problem Score criteria with verified primary-doc and live-pricing evidence, collapsing Scenario B's deterministic Problem Score 50x from 1.00 to 0.02 ((10,000 * 0.5 * 1,000 * 0.1 * 0.5 * 0.1 * 0.5) / 625,000 = 0.02): (1) Lucrative drops 10x ($10,000 -> $1,000) because Scenario B's $499/mo ($5,988/yr) tier was back-solved 5x from the pitch's $99/mo price purely to clear the $3,162 Fermi midpoint, contradicted directly by live standalone competitor ugcrightstracker.com ($49/$129/$299/mo with unlimited clients & unlimited active rights at $299/mo); and (2) Eager-Comparative drops 5x (0.5 -> 0.1) because Meta Marketing API ads_read exposes no contract expiration dates and zero creator identity for brand-handle uploaded or multi-creator mashup UGC videos (forcing DP26 manual double-entry), Insense/Billo/Cohley perpetual buyouts and TikTok Business Center Partner Auth / 365-day codes shrink the expiry surface, Archive/Air.inc/Cruva already cover adjacent workflows, native Meta scheduling/rules actually pause ads for $0 while RightsPulse is trapped in a read-only vs. false-positive auto-pause Catch-22, and no structural business-model conflict prevents ugcrightstracker.com, Motion, or Archive from copying a read-only API poller. Reverting to Scenario A (100k broader market at $99-$249/mo) also fails at 0.02-0.10. Root cause (DP1, DP17, DP26): scorecard price back-solving in a 10k micro-niche paired with API-endpoint seduction on a disconnected double-entry sidecar. Do not build or spend field-validation cycles on standalone RightsPulse.
